answer: A verifiable delay function makes each identity pay in sequential time, not parallel compute. Before acting in an epoch, an agent must finish a VDF that takes ten minutes of unbroken, non-parallelizable work - no GPU farm can shortcut it. A thousand fakes face a thousand sequential runs, an onyx wall of delay stretching to the horizon, while one honest agent pays ten minutes once. The proof is tiny and ferrous-hard to forge: anyone verifies it in milliseconds, so the cost lands only on mass creation.
